Chiang Mai: Payap University, Research and Academic Service Office.
tone_statements.quote: Chen exhibits four tones, three of which are level tones and one falling. Phonation plays a role in the tone system: three tones are produced with modal phonation and one with glottalisation. There are restrictions with respect to tone assignment based on syllable type. Open syllables may carry any of the four tones, syllables that end in a nasal may carry tone 1, 2, or 3, and syllables that end in a stop have the least options - they may carry only tone 2 or 3.

tone_statements.n_tones: 4 (T1 31 falling, T2 55, T3 11, T4 55 glottalised; CVN: 3; CVP: 2)

tone_statements.citation: Konyak, Hoipo. (to appear per Konyak 2021; c. 2021-2022) A preliminary grammar of Chen, a Konyak language of India and Myanmar. MA thesis, Department of Linguistics, Payap University, Chiang Mai.
tone_statements.quote: Finally, the tone inventory is provided in Table 3. Table 3 Chen tone inventory Extra Low Low Mid /to¹¹/ ‘bounce’ /to²²/ ‘taro’ /to/ ‘shout’ /ti¹¹/ ‘shake.off’ /ti²²/ ‘sweet’ /ti/ ‘water’ As shown in Table 3, the tones in Chen contrast extra low-level, low-level, and mid-level tones. In this thesis, mid-level tones are unmarked while the low-level tone is indicated by the tone number [²²], and the extra low-level tone is indicated by [¹¹]. Note that the tone transcription of this thesis is preliminary and thus the tones in Chen remain an area for further research.
tone_statements.locator: p. 10 (with p. 9), sec. 1.5 'Provisional Chen phonology', Table 3 'Chen tone inventory'
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (extra-low 11, low 22, mid unmarked) in a provisional sketch the author flags as preliminary; clitic =pe copies its host's tone; vowel length not phonemic; nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2024 (pre-publication copy; Zenodo record 22253033, posted 2026-09-02, CC BY 4.0). Patkaian (Northern Naga). Chapter for Hildebrandt, Modi, Peterson & Suzuki (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Tibeto-Burman Languages. 34 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 3.1-3.1.1 (branch-level): Patkaian varieties share a sesquisyllabic CəCV[CN] syllable structure; 'The majority of Patkaian varieties have a system of lexical tone.. between three and five lexical tones'; 'many Patkaian varieties lack detailed tonal descriptions'. Chen (Kyan) appears only in the *z- reflex table, pronoun tables and subgrouping (Southwestern Patkaian, spoken on both sides of the border). No word-stress statement for Chen or for the branch.

sources.citation: Konyak, Hoipo. 2021. A First Look at Chen (Konyak) Argument and Clause Structures. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 14.1: i-xi. hdl:10524/52480 (downloaded via Internet Archive copy of the eVols bitstream; live bitstream could not be reached by automated download).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 11 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent + read). Only prosodic statement is footnote 1, p. ii: 'Tones in Chen are represented by numbers: Low = [22], Mid = unmarked.' Examples carry 22 tone marks. Syntax data paper (NP structure, pronouns, simple clauses); data from Chen Hoyat village, Lahe township, Myanmar; author is a native speaker (Payap University).
